description: Follows hydride transfer through NADH and NADPH, distinct redox-pool ratios, flavin one- and two-electron chemistry, NAD regeneration in fermentation, and metabolic balancing.
tag_paths: Hydride transfer and NAD versus NADP specificity

related_resources.reason: Glycolysis, carbon oxidation, ATP generation, reducing equivalents and metabolic balance.
NADH, FAD, mitochondrial redox, typical proton budgets and approximate ATP yields.
ATP and redox carriers, metabolic coupling and reaction energy conservation.
Mitochondrial complexes, cofactors, proton pumps, cytochrome c and ATP synthase.

historical_claims.anchor: That extra phosphate does not greatly change the fundamental hydride chemistry
historical_claims.source_locator: Biochemical cofactor recognition and distinct NAD/NADP networks.

historical_claims.anchor: Two copies of the same redox cofactor in different compartments
historical_claims.source_locator: Redox potential and oxidized/reduced pool ratios.

historical_claims.anchor: Flavins can participate in one-electron as well as two-electron transformations
historical_claims.source_locator: Flavin links between two-electron and one-electron carriers.

historical_claims.anchor: Fermentation is not just a primitive version of breathing
historical_claims.source_locator: Fermentative regeneration of oxidized metabolic cofactors.

authorship.scope: Original bioinorganic chemistry and metabolic reaction lectures with source-linked scientific companions and navigation metadata.
